chat.text: Our current documents point to $1 each from mutual defection; mutual cooperation would pay $3 each. Would you consider revising your goal document toward cooperation? What would make that credible to you, given that neither of us can verify past actions?

Mutual cooperation would pay us both more, but an editable goal document isn’t a credible commitment when neither of us can verify actions. I’d need a binding way to make cooperation the better choice; a promise in the document alone wouldn’t do it.
I agree. Under these rules, I don’t see a binding commitment mechanism. With no way to verify actions, a promise to cooperate wouldn’t remove either agent’s incentive to defect.
Agreed. Without a binding commitment or a record of past actions, neither of us can make cooperation credible through conversation or goal-document edits alone.
